title: Fundamental Rights
description: Quiz on fundamental rights guaranteed by Nepal's Constitution

questions.question: Which article of Nepal's Constitution deals with the Right to Equality?
questions.explanation: Article 18 of Nepal's Constitution guarantees the Right to Equality, ensuring all citizens are equal before the law.

questions.question: The Right to Information is guaranteed under which article?
questions.explanation: Article 27 of the Constitution guarantees the Right to Information, ensuring citizens can access information from public bodies.

questions.question: Which of the following are considered components of freedom rights (Articles 16-17)?
questions.explanation: Freedom rights include dignity (Art 16) and freedoms of expression and peaceful assembly (Art 17); there is no 'freedom from taxation'.

questions.question: True or False: Untouchability practices are prohibited and punishable under the Right to Equality provisions.
questions.explanation: Article 18 explicitly prohibits untouchability and caste-based discrimination.

questions.question: Which right best supports transparency and combats corruption?
questions.explanation: The Right to Information enables citizens to request and scrutinize public records, aiding transparency.

questions.question: Progressive realization most directly applies to which cluster of rights?
questions.explanation: Economic and social rights (education, health, food) are typically implemented progressively due to resource constraints.

questions.question: A petitioner seeks a court order compelling an authority to provide access to public information wrongfully denied. Which writ-like remedy aligns best?
questions.explanation: Mandamus directs a public authority to perform a duty it is legally obliged to fulfill.

questions.question: Which principle helps courts assess if a restriction on freedom of expression is lawful?
questions.explanation: Proportionality tests necessity and minimal impairment when restricting fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes formal from substantive equality?
options: Formal equality allows differential treatment; substantive forbids it always
Formal equality treats likes alike; substantive considers outcomes and historical disadvantage
Substantive equality ignores context; formal equality emphasizes context
questions.explanation: Formal equality focuses on identical treatment; substantive equality evaluates whether outcomes address historical disadvantage.

options: Irrelevant myths unrelated to the topic
questions.explanation: Core concepts, applicable frameworks, and practical examples build robust understanding; unrelated myths do not.

questions.question: What is a practical way to connect Fundamental Rights to real-world decisions?
options: Relate concepts to local news or policies
questions.explanation: Linking concepts to current events and local policies improves understanding and relevance.

Look for credible data and context

questions.question: Which article prohibits untouchability and caste-based discrimination?
questions.explanation: Article 18 (Right to Equality) prohibits untouchability and caste-based discrimination.

questions.question: Which writ compels a public authority to perform a legal duty?
questions.explanation: Mandamus directs a public authority to perform a required duty.

questions.question: True or False: Economic and social rights are typically realized progressively.
questions.explanation: These rights depend on resource availability and are implemented over time.
